title: Generalized Symmetries of QED$_4$ on Non-Spin Manifolds
abstract: Generalized symmetries are sensitive to the tangential structure of spacetime. We study this interplay for massless QED on oriented non-spin four-manifolds, where the photon becomes a spin$^c$ connection and the path integral sums over spin$^c$ structures. The shifted flux quantization extends the magnetic 1-form symmetry into a $w_2$-twisted 1-form symmetry: its $2π$ rotation acts as a gravitational sign, fixed by the normal bundle of the surface the operator wraps. The obstruction to treating it as an ordinary magnetic 1-form symmetry is an order-two mixed magnetic-gravitational anomaly, which is classified by reduced oriented bordism and detected on the Wu manifold. In a fixed spin$^c$ sector, this anomaly is removable by a counterterm, so it is a property of the sum over spin$^c$ structures. We discuss its consequences for gapped, Coulomb, and Higgs phases. The chiral anomaly is governed by the index of the spin$^c$ Dirac operator, so rational chiral defects carry gravitational as well as electromagnetic responses. A spin$^c$ Hall topological field theory cancels the electromagnetic part but leaves a framing anomaly. At the level of anomaly inflow, this is canceled for every rational angle by stacking a neutral, generally noninvertible Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev layer. The same framing subtlety affects the chiral defects of QED on curved spin manifolds. The complex projective plane illustrates each of these features explicitly.
summary: This theoretical paper studies generalized symmetries in $	ext{QED}_4$ on non-spin manifolds, where the theory must account for the summation over all possible spin$^c$ structures. The core finding is the existence of a mixed magnetic-gravitational anomaly, which dictates how symmetries are preserved or modified by the geometry of spacetime. This work utilizes advanced TQFT and index theory to constrain the possible physical phases of the system.
main_problem: The paper investigates how generalized symmetries of Quantum Electrodynamics ($	ext{QED}_4$) are modified when the underlying spacetime manifold is non-spin, forcing the theory to sum over all possible spin$^c$ structures.
main_result: The analysis reveals an order-two mixed magnetic–gravitational anomaly, which is classified by reduced oriented bordism, and demonstrates that the full symmetry structure requires complex completion involving Witten–Reshetikhin–Turaev layers.
method: The authors employ advanced techniques from topological quantum field theory (TQFT), index theory (Dirac operator), and algebraic topology (bordism theory) to analyze symmetry constraints.
model_or_system: The primary model is massless $	ext{QED}_4$ studied on oriented non-spin four-manifolds. The analysis extends to studying chiral defects on lower-dimensional submanifolds, incorporating the concept of a spinc connection.
key_observables: The mixed magnetic–gravitational anomaly, the residual framing anomaly, and the index of the spin$^c$ Dirac operator.
important_parameters: The rational chiral rotation angle ($\alpha = 2\pi p/N$), and the structure of the manifold (non-spin, oriented).
main_assumptions: The theory is analyzed in the path integral sum over all spin$^c$ structures, and the anomaly cancellation requires the noncanonical addition of a WRT layer.
paper_structure: The paper systematically progresses from reviewing spin QED defects to analyzing the spinc structure and flux quantization, then deriving the mixed anomaly, and finally completing the symmetry structure via the Hall TFT and WRT layers.
why_interesting: The deep connection between topological invariants (like bordism classes) and fundamental symmetries in gauge theories provides a powerful mathematical framework applicable to understanding topological phases in condensed matter systems, such as those exhibiting fractional quantum Hall effects.
